content.comment_body: Hello, I've reviewed the [product_name] manual but still have questions about sending SMS messages. Is it possible to configure [product_name] to send an SMS when a memory flag, like M60, switches from 0 to 1 in [product_name] [version_no]? Or is a physical input required for the module to send SMS? Additionally, my [product_name] [version_no] was previously set with IP address 192.168.0.3 and this caused an error (blinking red light) on [product_name]. After changing the IP to 192.168.40 in the network settings, the blinking stopped, but I can't access 192.168.0.3 via my browser. It seems the module's IP might not be 192.168.0.3, and I'm unsure how to determine its current IP. I tried using IPCONFIG to locate the MAC address on my network but couldn't find it, even when it is connected to [product_name] [version_no] via Profinet. Any idea what's causing this?
Yes, it is possible. The procedure you need to follow is outlined in the manual.
Thank you. I'll go over the manual again and try to better understand it. Could you also provide advice on resolving the second issue?
You might want to use an Advanced IP scanner, which is available as free software.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unsure how to configure [product_name] to send SMS messages triggered by a memory flag change in [product_name] [version_no] instead of a physical input. Additionally, the user is having trouble identifying and accessing the module's IP address following changes to the network setup, leading to uncertainty about device discovery and connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to trigger SMS messages based on a memory flag change within [product_name] [version_no] and to be able to reliably locate and connect to the [product_name] module after making configuration changes to the network.
